source_reviews.independent_solution: Source 94 asks to construct the graphs of (a) y=6/x and (b) xy=-12. Definitions 11 and 14 make a graph the set of every real coordinate pair satisfying its equation; definition 15 classifies xy=k with k!=0 as a hyperbola. For (a), multiplying by its nonzero x gives xy=6, and the full graph is {(x,6/x): x is real, x!=0}. It contains (2,3),(-2,-3), has one branch for all x>0 in quadrant I and another for all x<0 in quadrant III. For (b), a nonzero product excludes both x=0 and y=0 and gives the full graph {(x,-12/x): x is real, x!=0}. It contains (3,-4),(-3,4), with branches in quadrants IV and II respectively. For both, |x| increasing without bound sends y towards zero without reaching it; x tending to zero from either side sends |y| to infinity. Thus x=0 and y=0 are asymptotes, neither axis has graph points, and both signed branches belong to each complete graph. The coordinate products must be 6 and -12, not merely positive and negative: (2,30) and (3,-40), for example, describe products 60 and -120. This solution was derived from the allowed seed and definitions before reading the view or internal rationale; no approved old solution was reused.
